title: Annotating your own games before the engine

D0.outcome: Explains annotating before the engine: critical moments and expected plans come first, then the comparison.

D1.outcome: After a game, marks two or three critical moments and the plan he expected for each side before any engine output.

D2.outcome: Annotates five games in a row unprompted, marking critical moments and expected plans before any engine output, and states the gap to the engine in one sentence per moment.

D3.outcome: Separates 'what I saw' from 'what was there' on at least three positions per game, with variations written.

misconceptions: The engine's best move is the explanation.
An annotation is a list of results.
sources: sources/sheets/capablanca_chess-fundamentals.md §6 (candid self-annotation in Part II as a model), CI-51
docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S9 (GAME.OWN T1 reflection to T3 protocol)
conditions: The learner marks critical moments and predicted plans before engine output.
The record is of what the learner saw and thought, including his own errors.
contrasts: Reading the engine's best move as an explanation.
Taking the champion's explanations of his own play as final diagnoses.
A game decided by an obvious early blunder with no critical moment to mark.
